p.i: traque in suæ matris domum: rependat vobis Iova pietatem, qua tum erga mortuos, tum erga me usæ estis. Faxit Iova ut quietem suum utraque apud maritum nanciscamini[?]. Hæc cùm locuta, eas deoscularetur, illa in lachrymas erumpentes, affirmabant, sese cum ipsa ad ejus populares esse reversuras. Sed Noemis eas ita hortata est: Revertimini meæ filio-læ, cur me comitemini? Nunquid ego adhuc in utero gesto filios, qui vobis futuri sint viri? Revertimini meæ filiolæ, discedite: nam ego quidè grandior sum, quàm ut sim apta viro. Quod si maximè spem esse putarem, virōq; vel in proximam noctem tradita, filios gignerem, an estis expectatura, donec adoleverint, & tam diu sine viris duratura? Non ita, meæ filiæ. Equidem valde vestra causa doleo, sed me Iova manus urget. Tum illa ploratum integrant, & Orphasocrum suam osculata, ei valedicit. At Rutha cum ea harebat, &c. Ruth.I.
Interea dum apud socrum manet, Noemis cum ea sic locuta est: Requiem tibi,

page.notes: The text reads "Orphafocrum", which is most likely "Orpha socrum" with the long s set as f and the space missing; I have written "Orphasocrum" with plain s, and the printed spacing is uncertain. "Rutha" is printed as such (the book's spelling of Ruth's name). The line "nancisc amini" may hold a printed line-end hyphen that is not clear on the scan, hence the [?]. The bare numeral at the middle of the page is rendered "LXXIII." as read from the spaced letters, which may actually be LXXIIII. A small stray dot in the left margin beside "popularés" is a blot or stain, not a marginal note, and is left out. The final word "mea" stands alone at the lower right and is recorded as the catchword. No marginal notes are printed on this page.
